structure:
repos/trade-imports-performance-tests (on main) is the k6 performance suite for INS. It runs against the stack rather than in it. The entry scripts are src/suites/*.k6.js (12 suites: smoke, average-load, peak-day, sustained-peak, p99-burst, spike-recovery, endurance, resilience, breakpoint-stubs, background-volume, health-check, combined). Each builds one run through src/k6/design-target.js (584 lines), which wires the journeys, readiness, faults, stub ceilings, eventing and summaries together. src/k6 holds 27 files and 5,599 lines; src/config and src/lib hold the endpoint catalogue, test data and the helpers the k6 modules call. The routes the scripts request from the services in scope sit in three groups. (1) The INS front door: the INS home at '/' (endpoint 'ins-dashboard'), sign-in, and the address book list, search, add, view, edit and delete pages (src/k6/front-door.js 453 lines, src/k6/readiness.js 137, src/lib/address-book.js 93, src/config/smoke.js 121). (2) The notification lifecycle in the animals frontend: the live-animals set root '/live-animals' and its notification list (the 'animals-dashboard' and dashboard search), creating a draft at '/live-animals/notifications', the notification hub, the notification view, declaration, confirmation, amend, cancel-amend, and the returning visit that re-opens a page after a session expires (src/k6/journeys.js 552, src/k6/returning-session.js 123, src/k6/browser-session.js 317, src/k6/pages.js 172, src/lib/redirects.js 120, src/config/journey-endpoints.js 102 for the shared endpoint names). (3) The live-animals journey pages the walker fills: origin, commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification, additional-details, accompanying-documents with upload and scan status, addresses with the party picker, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries and transporters (src/k6/live-animals.js 235, src/k6/journey-pages.js 167, src/k6/documents.js 149, src/lib/form-fill.js 133, src/lib/forms.js 52, src/lib/documents.js 95, src/config/test-data.js 74). The scope leaves out: the high-risk plants journey (src/k6/high-risk-plants.js and the 'high-risk-plants' half of journey-endpoints.js), which requests the plants frontend rather than the animals frontend or the INS front door; the backend, stub, reference-data, eventing, dead-letter, resilience, stub-ceiling, call-count and background-volume probes, which call services directly rather than frontend routes; the thresholds, SLAs, traffic model and summary-text config; and the suites' run shapes, which say how hard each route is driven, not which route it is.

Extracted in 3 parts:
Part 1, INS front door and address book: Part 1, INS front door and address book. Read in full: src/k6/front-door.js (453 lines: opening the INS home at '/', the dashboard-only session, the address-book session that adds, searches, views, edits and deletes an address, and the setup that makes the performance-test address findable under every declared role), src/k6/front-door.test.js (8 unit tests of the add helper and the setup), src/k6/readiness.js (137 lines: the readiness probes, two of which open INS pages and check their headings), src/lib/address-book.js (93 lines: the address book path, address types, declared roles, endpoint names, list and search path builder, worst-case search term), src/lib/address-book.test.js (its unit tests), src/config/smoke.js (121 lines: the stub identity, readiness timings, the perf address, the address-book load name prefix and the INS scenarios' endpoint lists) and src/config/trader-organisation.js (the organisation header). Also looked up WORST_CASE_SEARCH_LENGTH in src/config/test-data.js. Covered: the INS home route and its checks; every address-book route (list, address-type tab, role narrowing, search with q, worst-case search, address-type start page, add-address save, view, edit, delete); the readiness INS probes with their headings; the address types, declared roles and refusal messages; the perf address, load name prefix and trader organisation header. The JOURNEYS and live-animals/high-risk-plants scenario entries in smoke.js belong to other parts and are claimed only where they name INS endpoints.
Part 2, Live-animals set root and notification lifecycle: Part 2 read in full: src/k6/journeys.js (the notification run every journey shares: INS sign-in, journey dashboard, create, draft chunks across sessions, re-edit, submit through the declaration, read back, amend then cancel or resubmit, backend replay of the first save), src/k6/returning-session.js (the endurance returning visit), src/k6/browser-session.js and its test (cookie jar, manual redirect following, sign-in hops, stub credential post, stale-save counting, page parsing of crumb, heading, hidden fields, form inputs and upload target), src/k6/pages.js (the walker: request-mix classification, think time, counters), src/lib/redirects.js and its test (path and origin reading, localhost aliasing, staleAction=1 detection, the /oauth2/authresp sign-in page, the sign-in hop paths /auth/, /oauth2/, /idphub/, /organisations, and reading the new id after /live-animals/notifications/), src/config/journey-endpoints.js (sharedEndpoints and journeyEndpoints only) and the live-animals entry of JOURNEYS in src/config/smoke.js. Pages covered: the live-animals set root '/live-animals' (animals-dashboard) and its '?referenceNumber=<id>' search (animals-dashboard-search), POST '/live-animals/notifications' (animals-create) landing on '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/origin', the hub '/live-animals/notifications/<id>' (animals-hub), notification-view, declaration and its save (declaration=confirmed) landing on '/confirmation', POST '<base>/amend' landing on notification-view, cancel-amend and its save landing on notification-view with cancelled=1, and resubmission through the declaration. The live-animals returning visit re-opens '/live-animals'. The question pages between create and review are part 3's; the plants half of the same files is out of scope. The page-path helper pagePath (src/k6/journey-pages.js:72, '<base>/<slug>') and the returning-animals entry (src/config/design-target.js:346) were looked up only to resolve paths these files use.
Part 3, Live-animals journey pages: Part 3, live-animals journey pages. Read in full: src/k6/live-animals.js (the LIVE_ANIMALS_STEPS draft list of 12 steps, reEdit, amendEdit, planFor), src/k6/live-animals.test.js (2 tests), src/k6/journey-pages.js (save check, choice readers, page path, party picker with worst-case search, reachAndSubmit), src/k6/documents.js (accompanying-documents upload to cdp-uploader and scan-status poll), src/lib/form-fill.js and its test (blank-field fill rules, select options, species filter, d/m/yyyy date text), src/lib/forms.js and its test (hidden fields, prefilled fields, urlencoded body), src/lib/documents.js and its test (PDF and JPEG bytes, sizes, filenames, scan status settled and rejected), src/config/test-data.js (commodity search, worst-case search length, document issue date, scan poll and timeout, scan allowance, local stand-ins; its plants origins and potato arrival time belong to the plants journey, outside this source's scope) and the 'live-animals' entry of STEP_ENDPOINTS in src/config/journey-endpoints.js. Covered, in step order: origin, commodities (search then species), import-reason, consignment-details, commodities/identification, additional-details, accompanying-documents (upload and scan), addresses (5 party pickers), cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries (add then save), transporters; then reEdit, amendEdit and planFor, the endpoint tag names and the form-fill mechanics the steps rely on. Every path is relative to the notification base, which part 2 claims. The scripts read form names, option values and two radio labels; they read no headings, hints or error messages.

claims.statement: The scripts open the INS home at the path '/' of the INS frontend and name that request the 'ins-dashboard' endpoint.
A session reaching the INS home unsigned is signed in on the way, through the Defra ID identity provider, before the home page answers.
claims.quote: Opens the INS dashboard, which signs the session in on the way.

claims.statement: The scripts expect the signed-in INS home to answer HTTP 200 with the page heading 'Dashboard'.
claims.quote:
'INS dashboard opens signed in': (dashboardPage) =>
      dashboardPage.status === HTTP_OK && dashboardPage.heading === 'Dashboard'

claims.statement: The scripts check that sign-in to the INS home went through Defra ID, and record that sign-in as a page request of its own.
The scripts read nothing from the INS home beyond its status and heading: a dashboard-only session signs in and then re-opens '/' repeatedly as its only page.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any read of the dashboard's content in front-door.js; the address-book session goes from the home straight to the address book path rather than following a link.

claims.statement: The front-door scenario requests two endpoints: 'sign-in' and 'ins-dashboard'.
The address book lives at the INS path '/address-book'.
An address-book session opens the INS home first, then the address book list at '/address-book' (endpoint 'ins-address-book').
The address book has two address types, each a tab of the list: ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR and DESTINATION_CONSIGNEE_OR_IMPORTER.
An address type's tab is the list path with the query parameter addressType, such as '/address-book?addressType=ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR'.
A tab can be narrowed to one role with the query parameter role, placed after addressType.
claims.note: The doc comment calls it 'the `role` parameter the tab declares'.

claims.statement: A free-text search on a tab is the URL-encoded term in the query parameter q, placed after addressType and any role.
The ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR address type carries the roles PLACE_OF_ORIGIN and CONSIGNOR.
The DESTINATION_CONSIGNEE_OR_IMPORTER address type carries the roles CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER and PLACE_OF_DESTINATION.
Every address type has at least one declared role, so adding under every type reaches every role.
claims.quote: 'declares the roles %s carries, so a setup adding under every declared type reaches it'

claims.statement: An address-book session works on the ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR tab.
Adding an address starts at '/address-book/add/address-type?start=true', the address type page (endpoint 'ins-address-type').
The address type page is a form whose field addressType takes one of the address types; saving it (endpoint 'ins-address-type-save') leads to the add-address form.
The add-address form offers the roles of the chosen address type as checkboxes named 'roles'.
When the add-address form does not offer every role declared for its address type, the scripts stop with an error naming the address type, the roles not offered and the roles offered.
claims.quote: `The add form for "${addressType}" does not offer ${notOffered.join(', ')} — it offers ${offeredRoles.join(', ')}`

claims.statement: The add-address form is posted (endpoint 'ins-address-add-save') with the address fields, a name, and every role declared for the address type ticked.
The add-address form's fields, as the scripts post them, are name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone and email, with roles.
claims.quote:
name: 'Perf Test Holding',
  addressLine1: '4 Nursery Lane',
  addressLine2: '',
  townOrCity: 'Perth',
  county: '',
  postcode: 'PH1 5EX',
  countryCode: 'GB',
  phone: '01738 555 0143',
  email: 'perf@example.co.uk'
claims.note: Field names inferred from the perf address object the scripts spread into the add-address answers; addressLine2 and county are posted empty, so they are optional.

claims.statement: A successful add-address save lands, with HTTP 200, on the list tab of the address type it was added under.
The scripts check an added address by its name appearing in the text of the tab the save lands on.
A refused add-address save stays on the add form, '/address-book/add/address', answering 400 with the heading 'There is a problem', in the scripts' model of it.
claims.quote:
status: 400,
  url: '/address-book/add/address',
  heading: 'There is a problem'
claims.note: From a unit-test fake, not a request to the service; it implies the add-address form's path is '/address-book/add/address'.

claims.statement: An address-book session saves its address under the name 'Address Book Load <virtual user>-<iteration>'.
After adding, a session finds its address by searching the ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR tab for its name (endpoint 'ins-address-book-search').
Each address in a list or search result links to '/address-book/<address id>', and the scripts read the address id from the first such link.
A list page also links to the add-address start page and may link to an address's edit page and to further pages with a 'page' parameter; none of those counts as an address link.
claims.note: From unit-test inputs, which suggest the list offers pagination ('?page=2') and edit links; the scripts never request them.

claims.statement: When the search for its name finds no address, the session's 'address found by name' check fails and the session stops there.
An address's view page is '/address-book/<address id>' (endpoint 'ins-address-view'), and the scripts expect it to answer 200 and show the address's name.
An address's edit page is '/address-book/<address id>/edit' (endpoint 'ins-address-edit'), a form pre-filled with the address's current answers.
claims.note: Pre-filled is inferred: the session posts the form's own values back with only townOrCity changed.

claims.statement: A session edits its address by changing the town or city to 'Dundee' and saving (endpoint 'ins-address-edit-save').
A saved edit returns the user, with HTTP 200, to the address book list at '/address-book'.
Deleting an address opens a confirmation page at '/address-book/<address id>/delete' (endpoint 'ins-address-delete') and posts it with no answers (endpoint 'ins-address-delete-save').
After a delete the user lands, with HTTP 200, on a page that no longer links to the deleted address.
An address-book session leaves nothing behind in the address book: it deletes the address it added.
claims.quote: Leaves nothing behind in the book.

claims.statement: A share of address-book sessions runs a worst-case search on the ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR tab before adding, and expects it to answer 200.
The worst-case search term is 255 characters long: 'Worst case search ' padded with x, matching no address name the suite adds.
claims.note: Implies the address search accepts a 255-character term without refusing it.

claims.statement: The address-book scenario requests the endpoints sign-in, ins-dashboard, ins-address-book, ins-address-book-search, ins-address-type, ins-address-type-save, ins-address-add-save, ins-address-view, ins-address-edit, ins-address-edit-save, ins-address-delete and ins-address-delete-save, each a name in the endpoint catalogue.
claims.quote:
list: 'ins-address-book',
  worstCaseSearch: 'ins-address-book-search',
  typePage: 'ins-address-type',
  typeSave: 'ins-address-type-save',
  addSave: 'ins-address-add-save',
  search: 'ins-address-book-search',
  view: 'ins-address-view',
  edit: 'ins-address-edit',
  editSave: 'ins-address-edit-save',
  delete: 'ins-address-delete',
  deleteSave: 'ins-address-delete-save'

claims.statement: Before a run, setup makes the performance-test address findable under every declared role: for each address type it searches the tab narrowed to each role for the address's name.
Setup adds one record under an address type only when some role of that type does not find the address, ticking every role of the type; a type whose roles all find it gets no add.
claims.quote: 'adds under a type ticking every declared role when only some of its roles are found'

claims.statement: Setup logs which address types it added the performance-test address under, or that it was already found under every declared role.
claims.quote:
`Performance-test address added under: ${typesNeedingAnAdd.join(', ')}`
      : 'Performance-test address already found under every declared role'

claims.statement: When an add under a type does not land on that type's tab, or a role still does not find the address after the add, setup stops with an error listing, per address type, the roles still missing or the status and heading of the page the save landed on.
claims.quote: `Could not make the performance-test address found by every declared role: ${messages.join('; ')}`
claims.note: Each message is `${addressType}: ${roles.join(', ')}` or `${addressType}: save answered ${status} "${heading}"`.

claims.statement: The performance-test address is 'Perf Test Holding', 4 Nursery Lane, Perth, PH1 5EX, country GB, phone 01738 555 0143, email perf@example.co.uk.
claims.quote:
name: 'Perf Test Holding',
  addressLine1: '4 Nursery Lane',
  addressLine2: '',
  townOrCity: 'Perth',
  county: '',
  postcode: 'PH1 5EX',
  countryCode: 'GB',
  phone: '01738 555 0143',
  email: 'perf@example.co.uk'

claims.statement: Setup's address-book requests carry the readiness tags, phase 'readiness' and name 'readiness', which keep them out of every threshold.
The readiness probe 'INS signed-in page' opens '/' (page name 'ins-dashboard') signed in and expects HTTP 200 with the heading 'Dashboard'.
The readiness probe 'address book read' opens '/address-book' (page name 'ins-address-book') signed in and expects HTTP 200 with the heading 'Address book'.

Readiness also probes the reference data's '/countries' for a non-empty list, and each of the animals, plants and INS backends' '/notifications?page=1' for HTTP 200 with the trader's organisation header.
claims.note: Service calls rather than frontend routes; recorded because readiness.js is in this part's read list.

claims.statement: Readiness re-runs every probe every 5 seconds for up to 300 seconds, then stops the run with an error naming each probe still failing.
claims.quote: `The stack was not functionally ready within ${READINESS.timeoutSeconds}s: ${failed.join(', ')}`

claims.statement: A service call made as the trader carries the organisation in the header 'Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id'.
The scripts sign in as the stub identity with CRN 2100010101 in organisation 5900001, with the password from AUTH_PASSWORD or the stub's default.
claims.note: The stub's default password is [REDACTED] here.

claims.statement: The scripts follow at most 10 redirect hops per request.

The scripts never request a role-narrowed tab for the DESTINATION_CONSIGNEE_OR_IMPORTER type except during setup, and never open the address-book list without an address type except the bare '/address-book'; what the bare list shows (which tab is chosen by default) is not said.
claims.note: Looked in front-door.js, address-book.js and readiness.js: the bare list is checked only for its 'Address book' heading.

claims.statement: The live-animals journey's set root, the page a user starts from and returns to, is '/live-animals' on the animals frontend.
The first question page a new live-animals notification lands on after it is created is 'origin'.
The live-animals journey's requests are tagged with the endpoint prefix 'animals', and the journey is backed by trade-imports-animals-backend.
Opening the set root '/live-animals' as a signed-in user answers 200 with a page that carries a CSRF crumb in a 'csrf-token' meta tag; the run checks both.
claims.quote:
'journey dashboard opens with a crumb': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK && page.crumb !== ''

claims.statement: A request for the set root '/live-animals' is tagged as the 'animals-dashboard' endpoint and classified as a dashboard read in the request mix.
The notification list on the set root can be searched by reference number with the query parameter 'referenceNumber', as '/live-animals?referenceNumber=<id>'.

After a notification is submitted, searching the set root by its reference number answers 200 and the page text contains the notification's id; the run checks this as 'submitted notification is on the dashboard'.
claims.quote:
'submitted notification is on the dashboard': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK && page.html.text().includes(run.id)

claims.statement: A dashboard search request is tagged as the 'animals-dashboard-search' endpoint and classified as a dashboard read.
A user creates a new draft notification by posting a form to '/live-animals/notifications' that carries only the crumb read from the set root page.
Creating a draft redirects the user to '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/origin', and the run reads the new notification's id from the path segment after '/live-animals/notifications/'.
claims.quote:
'draft created through the frontend': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK &&
      id !== '' &&
      pathOf(page.url).endsWith(`/${run.journey.firstSavePage}`)

claims.statement: A draft notification's id has the form 'DRAFT.GB.<year>.<number>', as the example the tests read from a create redirect shows.
claims.note: The id format comes from a unit-test fixture, not a live response; the reconciler should not treat it as a ruled format.

claims.statement: When the create redirect does not land under '/live-animals/notifications/', no id is read and the run ends that notification.
claims.note: mechanism: the harness gives up on a notification whose create did not land on a notification path.

claims.statement: The create request is tagged as the 'animals-create' endpoint.
Each notification has a hub page at '/live-animals/notifications/<id>'.
A user who comes back in a later session to carry on a draft opens the notification's hub '/live-animals/notifications/<id>' first, after the set root, before the next question page.
A submitted notification's hub reads back with status 200; the run checks this as 'submitted hub reads back'.
claims.quote: check(hub, { 'submitted hub reads back': (page) => page.status === HTTP_OK })

claims.statement: A hub request is tagged as the 'animals-hub' endpoint.
Each notification has a review page at '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/notification-view', which the user opens before submitting.

The notification view page can carry a POST form with a hidden 'step' field; when it does, the user reaches the declaration by posting the view's hidden fields to '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/declaration'.
claims.quote:
const declaration = view.hiddenFields.step
    ? walker.post(declarationPath, view.hiddenFields, run.shared.declaration)
    : walker.reach(undefined, declarationPath, run.shared.declaration)

claims.statement: When the notification view has no hidden 'step' field, the user opens '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/declaration' directly with a GET.
claims.note: reach with no current page always opens the path, so this is a plain GET of the declaration page. The script supports both routes, so which one the frontend uses today is not settled here.

claims.statement: A submitted notification's view page reads back with status 200; the run checks this as 'submitted notification view reads back'.
claims.quote: 'submitted notification view reads back': (page) => page.status === HTTP_OK

claims.statement: The declaration page has a form field 'declaration', and the user submits it with the value 'confirmed', sent with the page's prefilled and hidden fields.
Saving the declaration lands the user on a page whose path ends '/confirmation', with status 200; the run checks this as 'submitted through the declaration page' for a first submission.
A notification counts as submitted only when the declaration save lands on '/confirmation' with status 200; it is counted as a 'first' submission or an 'amendment' resubmission.
The notification view, declaration and declaration save requests are tagged as 'animals-notification-view', 'animals-declaration' and 'animals-declaration-save'.
After a first submission, the user reads the notification back in order: the set root searched by reference number, then the hub, then the notification view.
A submitted notification is amended by posting a form carrying only the crumb, read from the dashboard search page, to '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/amend'.
Starting an amendment lands the user on the notification's view page '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/notification-view' with status 200; the run checks this as 'amendment started'.
After starting an amendment, the user edits one question page (the journey's named amend edit step) before either cancelling or resubmitting.
claims.quote:
const edit = run.draftSteps.find((step) => step.name === run.steps.amendEdit)
  const edited = runSteps(context, [edit], undefined)
claims.note: Which question page the amend edit is belongs to part 3's step definitions.

claims.statement: Answers typed during an amendment carry the suffix '-A', so an amended answer differs from the first one.
claims.note: mechanism: the suffix is passed into the step context; how each step applies it is part 3's.

claims.statement: An amendment can be cancelled from a page at '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/cancel-amend', which the user opens and then submits with no answers of its own, only its prefilled and hidden fields.
Confirming the cancel-amend page lands the user on the notification view with 'cancelled=1' in the URL, with status 200; the run checks this as 'amendment cancelled'.

An amendment that is not cancelled is resubmitted the same way as a first submission: notification view, then declaration confirmed, landing on '/confirmation'; the run checks this as 'amendment resubmitted'.
The amend, cancel-amend and cancel-amend save requests are tagged 'animals-amend', 'animals-cancel-amend' and 'animals-cancel-amend-save', and amendment pages are classified as amendment traffic.
Whether a notification is amended, and whether that amendment is cancelled or resubmitted, is drawn per notification from the traffic model.
The run models a notification's tail as 3 review pages and 3 read-back pages, plus 3 pages to start and edit an amendment and then 2 to cancel it or 3 to resubmit it.
claims.quote:
const REVIEW_PAGES = 3
const READ_BACK_PAGES = 3
const AMEND_START_AND_EDIT_PAGES = 3
const CANCEL_AMEND_PAGES = 2
const RESUBMIT_AMEND_PAGES = 3

claims.statement: A notification is drafted across one or more user sessions; each session signs in afresh through the INS front door, opens the INS dashboard, then opens the journey set root.
claims.quote:
Each session signs in afresh through the INS front door. The draft steps are
 * split across the sessions

claims.statement: One browser's cookie jar is shared between the INS frontend and the animals frontend within a user session, as one browser is across frontends.
claims.quote: @param {object} [options.jar] - A cookie jar to share with another session, as one browser does across frontends.

claims.statement: Before the last session submits, the user re-edits answered question pages until the notification reaches the traffic model's pages-per-notification figure.
claims.quote:
the last one also re-edits answered pages to
 * reach the pages-per-notification figure

claims.statement: Each user session ends with repeat opens of the INS dashboard '/' (endpoint 'ins-dashboard') as status checks, up to the front-door model's core pages per journey session.
Any step that does not answer 200 ends the notification's run there; later pages are not requested.
claims.quote: A step that does not land ends the iteration.
claims.note: mechanism: harness flow control over the notification lifecycle.

claims.statement: After the first save, the run reads the notification's fulfilments from the animals backend at GET '<backend>/notifications/<id>/fulfilments' and its list entry at GET '<backend>/notifications?referenceNumber=<id>', each expected to answer 200.
The run then replays the captured save to the animals backend with PUT '<backend>/notifications/<id>' as JSON, and expects 200 ('backend replay accepted the captured save').
claims.quote:
'backend replay accepted the captured save': (response) =>
      response.status === HTTP_OK
claims.note: mechanism: builds a replace body from the fulfilments and the first list entry ('content.0').

claims.statement: Backend requests carry the trader's organisation in headers built from the signed-in identity's organisation id.
The backend reads and replay are tagged 'animals-backend-fulfilments', 'animals-backend-list' and 'animals-backend-replace', of kind 'api'.
When the run is set to confirm event arrival and the journey publishes events, it proves after the notification is finished that its events reached the INS dashboard read model.
claims.quote: @param {boolean} [options.confirmsEventArrival] - True proves, once the notification is finished, that its events reached the dashboard read model.

claims.statement: The endpoint names every journey shares are: <prefix>-dashboard, -dashboard-search, -create, -hub, -notification-view, -declaration, -declaration-save, -amend, -cancel-amend and -cancel-amend-save.
A journey scenario can request 'sign-in', 'ins-dashboard', every shared endpoint, every step endpoint of the journey and the three backend endpoints, with no repeats.
The frontends sign a user in through a redirect chain; every hop whose path starts '/auth/', contains '/oauth2/' or '/idphub/', or is exactly '/organisations', is a sign-in hop.

The Defra ID stub's sign-in form sits at a path ending '/oauth2/authresp' (locally under '/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/'), and the user signs in there by posting the stub credentials crn and password as a form.
claims.quote:
if (response.status === HTTP_OK && isIdentitySignInPage(url)) {
        response = postForm(url, credentials, SIGN_IN_ENDPOINT)
claims.note: Credentials are [REDACTED] here; the stub identity's values live in src/config/smoke.js.

claims.statement: After a successful sign-in, the chain returns the user to the page they first asked for.
claims.quote:
're-authenticated and returned to the page it asked for': (landed) =>
      landed.status === HTTP_OK && pathOf(landed.url) === entry.path

claims.statement: In CDP the sign-in chain runs from the stub's '/oauth2/v2.0/authorize' to its '/oauth2/authresp' and back to the frontend's '/auth/callback?code=…&state=…', and the stub may show '/organisations' along the way.
claims.note: From test fixtures modelled on CDP dev URLs, not a live trace.

claims.statement: A chain that passes through sign-in hops and lands with 200 counts as a sign-in even when no credentials form is shown; a chain that reaches sign-in and ends in a server error does not.
claims.note: mechanism: counts sign-ins per session to tell sign-in from re-authentication.

claims.statement: Once a session has signed in once, every later sign-in hop is tagged as re-authentication.
A redirect chain is followed for at most 10 hops; a chain still redirecting after that is marked as too many redirects.
When a save is out of date, the frontend redirects the user back with 'staleAction=1' in the query; the run counts that as a handled outcome rather than an error.
claims.quote: The journey sends the user back with `staleAction=1` when a save is out of date.

claims.statement: A form save carries a 'concurrencyToken' hidden field; where a page has several POST forms, the one with a concurrency token is the one submitted.
claims.note: mechanism: picks the last POST form with a concurrencyToken, else the first POST form. That saves carry the token is inferred from the selector.

claims.statement: Frontends send redirects with browser-visible 'localhost' addresses and root-relative Location headers; relative Locations such as 'next' are not expected.
claims.note: mechanism: the harness swaps localhost for an alias when run in a container.

claims.statement: Each page the run reads exposes its first h1 heading, its crumb, the hidden fields and answer inputs of its chosen POST form, and the upload target of a file-carrying submit button.
claims.note: mechanism: page parsing; no script in this part checks a heading's text.

claims.statement: A form submit sends the page's prefilled answers and hidden fields back to the page's own URL, with the user's answers laid over them.
claims.note: mechanism: emulates a browser's form post.

claims.statement: Every page the user opens is followed by think time drawn around the journey's mean, unless the run is unpaced, and is counted toward the notification's pages.
claims.quote:
Every navigation a scenario makes goes through here, which is what keeps the
 * request mix honest and the load paced like a person's.

claims.statement: The run reports page requests by traffic class and frontend, dashboard read share, post-submission reads, amendment pages, pages per notification, session seconds, notifications started by type and notifications submitted by first or amendment.
Live animals has one notification type, 'live-animals', for splitting load.
claims.quote: @param {string} notificationType - `live-animals`, or a high-risk plants commodity type.

claims.statement: A returning live-animals user keeps one browser for the whole run and on each visit re-opens the set root '/live-animals'.
When the frontend's session has expired, the returning visit goes through Defra ID again and lands back on the set root; that sign-in is counted as a re-authentication and checked.
claims.quote:
when the frontend's session has expired the
 * visit goes through Defra ID again and lands back on the dashboard.

claims.statement: The run tells a session has expired when opening the page triggers a new sign-in; the first sign-in of a returning browser is recorded as sign-in, every later one as re-authentication.

With session expiry set to 'client', the returning browser forgets its cookies for the frontend once the session lifetime has passed since it last signed in, standing in for an expiry a compressed run cannot reach.
Each returning visit must land with status 200 ('returning visit landed') and is followed by a wait of the visit interval.
No script in this part checks the copy on the set root, hub, notification view, declaration, confirmation or cancel-amend pages: headings, captions, labels, buttons and messages are not asserted.
claims.note: Looked at every check() in journeys.js and returning-session.js: they assert status, path, crumb, cancelled=1 and the id in the page text only.

claims.statement: This part does not show what the set root's notification list shows when a reference number search finds nothing, nor any other filter or paging on the list.
claims.note: Only a search for a known submitted id is made.

claims.statement: This part does not show the fields of the cancel-amend page or the notification view beyond the hidden 'step' field, nor what the confirmation page shows.
claims.note: cancel-amend is submitted with {} answers; the confirmation is only checked by path.

claims.statement: The performance walker fills a live-animals notification draft in 12 steps, in this order: origin, commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification, additional-details, documents, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters.
claims.quote:
export const LIVE_ANIMALS_STEPS = Object.freeze({
  draft: [
    reachAndSubmit('origin', 'origin', ENDPOINTS.origin, originAnswers),
    commodities,
    reachAndSubmit(
      'import-reason', ... documentsStep,
    addresses,
    reachAndSubmit('cph-number', ... portOfEntry,
    transitCountries,
    transporters
  ]
claims.note: This is the order the perf walker visits pages, which its test says follows the order the journey offers them for the steps it checks; it is not proof of the frontend's own task-list order for every step.

claims.statement: Each step opens its page at the notification base path followed by the page's slug.
A step's save counts as saved only when it lands on a page that answered 200, with no redirect loop and no stale-save redirect; the check is named '<step> saved'.
The origin page is at '<base>/origin'.
The origin save sends countryOfOrigin, drawn at random from the options of the page's countryOfOrigin select, or 'FR' when the page offers none.
The origin page has a countryOfOrigin select whose option values are country codes such as 'FR'.
claims.note: Inferred: the script reads the select's options by that name and falls back to the code 'FR', so the options are codes.

claims.statement: The origin save answers regionOfOriginCodeRequirement with 'no'.
The origin save sends internalReferenceNumber as 'PERF-' followed by the virtual user, a hyphen, the iteration and a suffix.
The commodities page is at '<base>/commodities'.
On the commodities page the walker searches by submitting commoditySearch 'Bos taurus' with action 'search'.
The commodity search finds cattle by its Latin name 'Bos taurus', not by the word 'cow', because MDM finds it that way.
claims.quote:
// Cattle is the one commodity whose pages match the live-animals step list exactly. MDM finds it by its Latin name, not by "cow".
export const ANIMAL_COMMODITY_SEARCH = 'Bos taurus'

claims.statement: Cattle is the one commodity whose pages match the walker's live-animals step list exactly; other commodities show a different set of pages.
claims.quote: // Cattle is the one commodity whose pages match the live-animals step list exactly.
claims.note: The second half is inferred from 'the one commodity'.

claims.statement: After the search, the commodities page lists species choices named 'species' whose values are '<commodity code>|<Latin name>'.
claims.quote: @param {string[]} speciesValues - Species checkbox values, each `<commodity code>|<Latin name>`.

claims.statement: The commodities save sends one species value, drawn at random from the species listed under commodity code '0102'.
claims.quote:
species: pickFrom(
            context,
            speciesUnderCode(
              choiceValues(searched, 'species'),
              ANIMAL_COMMODITY_CODE
            )
          )

claims.statement: A search for 'Bos taurus' can list the same Latin name under several commodity codes (such as 0102, 05111000 and 01022100), and only the exact code 0102 is kept.
claims.ref: repos/trade-imports-performance-tests/src/lib/form-fill.test.js:speciesUnderCode 'keeps only the species under the code'
claims.note: The codes are a unit-test fixture, not read from a live page; they show the walker expects codes beyond 0102 for the same name.

claims.statement: The import-reason page is at '<base>/import-reason'.
The import-reason save sends reasonForImport 'internalMarket'.
The import-reason save sends purposeInInternalMarket 'breeding' on the same page as the reason for import.
claims.note: Both answers go in one save, so the purpose in the internal market is asked on the import-reason page itself.

claims.statement: The consignment-details page is at '<base>/consignment-details', and the walker answers every field it finds blank there.
The identification page is at '<base>/commodities/identification', and the walker answers every field it finds blank there.
The scripts do not name the fields of the consignment-details or identification pages: they fill whatever blank fields each page renders, so this source does not say which fields those pages ask.
claims.note: Looked in live-animals.js, form-fill.js and test-data.js. Only the fill rules by name pattern hint at the field names (numberOfAnimalsQuantity, numberOfPackages, a tag field).

claims.statement: The blank-field fill answers only empty text, search, number, tel, email, untyped and textarea fields, and leaves radios, checkboxes and fields that already hold a value alone.
claims.quote:
const isBlankTextField = ({ type, value, name }) =>
  TEXT_LIKE_TYPES.has(type ?? '') && !value && !SEARCH_FIELDS.has(name)
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's own form filler, working on the inputs read off a page.

claims.statement: The blank-field fill leaves search boxes named q, commoditySearch, search and referenceNumber empty.
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's form filler.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name starts 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity' is answered '1'.
claims.note: mechanism: the test shows the field is indexed per line, such as 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity-0'.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name starts 'numberOfPackages' is answered '5'.
claims.note: mechanism: the test names it 'numberOfPackages-0'.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name contains 'tag' is answered 'UK123456789012'.
claims.note: mechanism: the test names an 'earTag-0' field, an animal identification field.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name contains 'quantity' (other than numberOfAnimalsQuantity) is answered '5'.
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's form filler.

claims.statement: The fill rules also answer commodityCode '0602 20 20', eppoCode 'PIEAB' and species 'Picea abies', which are plant values shared with the plants journey.
claims.note: mechanism: one filler serves both journeys; these values matter for live animals only if a blank text field on a live-animals page has such a name.

claims.statement: Any other blank text field is answered 'PERF' followed by the virtual user and iteration, such as 'PERF37'.
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's form filler.

claims.statement: A select with nothing chosen is answered with its first option that is not the empty placeholder, and a select that already holds a value is left as it is.
claims.quote:
export const firstOption = (values) => values.find((value) => value) ?? ''

const selectAnswerEntries = (input, chooseOption) =>
  input.value ? [] : [[input.name, chooseOption(input.options)]]
claims.note: mechanism: implies the pages' selects start with an empty placeholder option.

claims.statement: The additional-details page is at '<base>/additional-details'.
The additional-details save sends animalsCertifiedFor, choosing the choice whose label contains 'Slaughter'.
The additional-details page offers 'animals certified for' as a radio or checkbox group with a choice labelled 'Slaughter'.
claims.note: Inferred: choiceLabelled reads input[name=animalsCertifiedFor] and matches label text containing 'Slaughter'.

claims.statement: The additional-details save sends containsUnweanedAnimals, choosing the choice whose label contains 'No'.
When no choice's label contains the wanted text, the walker picks the first choice the page lists.
claims.quote:
const wanted = inputs.find((input) => labelOf(page, input).includes(text))

claims.statement: The accompanying-documents page is at '<base>/accompanying-documents'.
Each uploaded document is given the reference 'PERFDOC<vu>V<iteration>N<number>', because the backend accepts a document reference of letters and digits only.
The document upload sends accompanyingDocumentReference with the document's reference.
The document upload sends accompanyingDocumentType, drawn at random from the options of the page's accompanyingDocumentType select.
The document upload sends accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue as a date 30 days before the run, written d/m/yyyy.
claims.note: test-data.js: '// Date of issue given to every uploaded document.\nexport const DOCUMENT_ISSUED_DAYS_AGO = 30'. The date is one text field, not day, month and year fields.

claims.statement: The document upload is sent with action 'add', together with the file, in one request.
The page's file-carrying button posts the document straight to the cdp-uploader and its virus scan, so the file's bytes never pass through the animals frontend.
claims.quote:
Each document goes straight to the real cdp-uploader and its virus scan,
 * which is where the page's own file-carrying button posts, so the bytes never
 * pass through the frontend.

claims.statement: After an upload, the upload service returns the browser to the accompanying-documents page, which takes the document on from there.
claims.quote:
The upload service returns the browser to the
 * page, which takes the document on from there.

claims.statement: An upload counts as done when the response is 200 and its URL, without query or fragment, ends at '<base>/accompanying-documents'.
The walker uploads PDF files (application/pdf, '.pdf') and JPEG files (image/jpeg, '.jpg'), named by the document reference.
claims.note: The mix of kinds and the size range come from the journey model, outside this part.

claims.statement: A document's size is drawn from a kilobyte range, counting a kilobyte as 1,000 bytes, as the animals frontend's upload limit counts.
claims.quote: A kilobyte is 1,000 bytes, as the animals frontend's upload limit counts.

claims.statement: The uploaded files start and end like a real PDF or JPEG and are padded in between.
claims.quote: It starts and ends like a real PDF or JPEG, and is padded in between.
claims.note: mechanism: synthetic test files for the upload.

claims.statement: The animals frontend serves a scan status route at '<base>/accompanying-documents/status' that returns JSON with a documents list, each with a scanStatus.
The accompanying-documents page's script polls the status route every 3 seconds, and the walker polls at the same interval.
claims.note: This is a JavaScript enhancement on the page; the source does not say what the page does without JavaScript.

claims.statement: A scan counts as settled once the status route lists at least one document and none has scanStatus 'PENDING'.
A document's scan status is one of 'PENDING', 'COMPLETE' or 'REJECTED', and both 'COMPLETE' and 'REJECTED' end the scan.
claims.ref: repos/trade-imports-performance-tests/src/lib/documents.js:11-12; src/lib/documents.test.js:scanHasSettled 'is true once every scan is complete or rejected'
claims.note: 'COMPLETE' appears only in the unit tests; the code knows only PENDING and REJECTED.

claims.statement: The run checks that no uploaded document's scan was rejected.
A scan still pending 120 seconds after the upload landed is recorded as stuck.
The document scan is judged against a P99 under 60 seconds, the allowance for upload pages.
claims.quote: 'Document scan allowance: P99 under 60s, as for upload pages (DR-EUDP-005 section 4.7, SYN-28, SYN-29)'

claims.statement: The run records how long each scan took as document_scan_duration and counts uploads as documents_uploaded.
claims.quote:
const scanDuration = new Trend('document_scan_duration', true)
const documentsUploaded = new Counter('documents_uploaded')

claims.statement: In a local run, document storage and virus scanning are the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan, so results depending on them are not CDP's.
claims.quote: "Stand-ins: SNS and SQS are floci, and document storage and virus scanning are the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan, so results that depend on them are not CDP's"

claims.statement: The accompanying-documents page continues with action 'continue'; with no documents to upload the walker only opens the page and continues.

With no documents the step only

claims.statement: The addresses page is at '<base>/addresses'.
From the addresses page the walker picks five parties, in this order: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and destination, each at '<base>/<party>/select'.
Each party picker is searched by submitting q with the performance-test address's name and action 'search'.
Each party picker is saved by sending the 'party' radio whose label names the performance-test address, with action 'save'.
A party picker's save lands back on the page the picker was opened from.
claims.quote: The picker's own save lands on the page it came from.

claims.statement: Search results on a party picker are listed as radios whose labels show the address's name.
claims.note: Inferred from the walker matching the address name in the radio labels.

claims.statement: Once per notification, while the worst-case search is pending, the first party picker is searched with a 255-character term before the real search, and the run checks it answered 200.
The longest searchable address field is 255 characters, the INS address book's name maximum length.
claims.quote:
// The longest searchable address field: ins-frontend features/address-book/fields.js FIELD_RULES.name.maxLength.
export const WORST_CASE_SEARCH_LENGTH = 255

claims.statement: After the five pickers the walker reopens the addresses page and saves it with no answers of its own.
The party pickers search the address book, so the addresses a live-animals notification uses come from the trader's address book.

claims.statement: The transporters page is at '<base>/transporters', and its save sends the first 'transporter' choice the page lists, with action 'save'.

claims.statement: When the walker re-edits a live-animals notification it reopens origin, import-reason, consignment-details, additional-details, cph-number and port-of-entry.
When the walker amends a submitted live-animals notification it edits the origin page.
Each live-animals run is planned with notificationType 'live-animals'.

Every live-animals page request is tagged with an endpoint name 'animals-<step>' for opening and 'animals-<step>-save' for saving, with '-search' for the commodity search and party picker, 'animals-documents-upload' and 'animals-documents-status' for documents, and 'animals-transit-countries-add' for adding a transit country.
claims.note: The thresholds and catalogue key on these names, so a step cannot send a request they do not know.

claims.statement: Each save posts the page's hidden fields with the answers on top, and leaves out any answer the page did not offer.
